3. It is argued by Ld. Addl PP for state/ Revisionist that revision petition may kindly be allowed and the order dated 24.06.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court may kindly be set-aside.
4.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for Respondent has opposed the contentions made by Ld.

Additional PP for state/revisionist and submits that as nothing was found incriminating against respondent and evidence collected by was not sufficient to form prima facie opinion against the respondent which enabled the Ld. Trial Court to discharge the respondent, therefore, the present revision petition may kindly be dismissed.

Digitally CR No. 322/2023 SUSHIL  SUSHIL KUMAR  KUMAR Date:

This Court have given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of ld.
Counsel for the revisionist/accused as well as Ld. APP for State / Respondent.
This Court has also perused the record.
6. In the present case, Trial Court Record has been summoned and the same has been carefully perused.

Perusal of the Trial Court Record shows that an FIR bearing no.230/2018 was registered under Section 7/10 Essential Commodities Act, 1955 at PS Adarsh Nagar and after completion of investigation, charge- sheet for the offences punishable U/s 420/409 IPC & under Section 7/10 Essential Commodities Act, 1955 was filed against accused Naresh Garg on 14.07.2021.
Perusal of the Trial Court Record further shows that after taking cognizance of the alleged offences, accused was summoned by Ld. Trial Court.

Perusal of Trial Court Record further shows that arguments on the point of charge was heard and vide impugned order dated 24.06.2023, respondent Naresh Garg was discharged by Ld. Trial Court for the offences punishable U/s 420/409 IPC & under Section 7/10 Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
7. It is important to mention that at the stage of framing of charge, Court has to see whether or not there is prima facie case against the accused.

In the present case, from perusal of the Trial Court Record, this Court is of view that Ld. Trial Court has rightly signed by CR No. 322/2023 SUSHIL SUSHIL KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.10.07 17:04:27 +0530 discharged respondent Naresh Garg and the impugned order dated 24.06.2023 is well reasoned and a detailed order.

Perusal of impugned order dated 24.06.2023, Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that IO did not examine any independent witness i.e. no Ration Card Holder has been examined by IO to verify the case of complainant that as per door to door survey report, Ration Card Holders who were found at the given address did not take the supplies from the accused's shop.

Further, Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that there is no evidence documentary / oral on record to show that variation of food supplies as alleged by State vs Naresh Garg on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108681584/
3 prosecution and that the stock register, cash memo and other documents which the complainant was allegedly not maintaining properly were never seized by the IO to show the lapse on the part of accused.
Further, that no indenpendent/public witness was examined to prima facie case against the accused and the E- POS system which respodent / accused alleged misused were never seized by IO.
8. In view of the above discusssion, this Court is of view that there is no illegality, infirmity or perversity in the impugned order dated 24.06.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court.
Same is accordingly upheld and the present revision petition is hereby dismissed.
9. A copy of this order be given to Revisionist and be also sent to the Ld. Trial Court along with the TCR immediately.
Digitally  signed by CR No. 322/2023 SUSHIL KUMAR  KUMAR
